summary.whatChanges: Zod v4's parse memoizer now stores its per-parse caches in WeakMap/WeakSet instead of Map/Set, so parsed input objects are no longer kept alive by the schema-attached bucket cache. A new test uses WeakRef plus a manually exposed V8 gc to assert the input is collectable after parsing a recursive schema.
behaviorChanges: Objects passed to parse() on recursive/memoized schemas are no longer retained after the parse finishes, so long-lived schemas stop accumulating memory.
Memoizer cache entries and back-edge records can be garbage collected mid-parse rather than living for the whole parse context.
Test suite adds a GC-dependent test that enables --expose-gc at runtime via v8.setFlagsFromString.
risks: WeakMap/WeakSet require object keys; any primitive or non-object value reaching bucket.get/set or backEdges.add would now throw instead of being cached.
Cache entries may be collected while still logically needed, potentially changing cycle-detection or memoization hits under memory pressure.
The new test depends on GC timing and v8.setFlagsFromString('--expose-gc'), which is inherently flaky and mutates process-wide V8 flags for the rest of the test run.
WeakRef is used although the stated compile target (es2020) lacks it, relying on a runtime cast.
